quests.instruction: Why do we walk instead of run in the hallway?
quests.correctAnswer: Someone could appear around a corner 🚶
options: Running is banned everywhere in school 🚫
Hallways are very short and need speed 📏
Someone could appear around a corner 🚶
quests.explanation: Hallways have doors and corners where people can't see you coming, so walking prevents collisions.
quests.funFact: Corners and doors are places where people can't see each other until the last moment.

quests.instruction: Which is the safest way to use stairs?
quests.correctAnswer: Hold the handrail and take one step at a time 🪜
options: Slide down the rail to save your legs 🛝
Hold the handrail and take one step at a time 🪜
Skip steps so you reach the bottom faster 💨
quests.explanation: Holding the rail and stepping carefully helps you keep your balance, even if someone bumps you.
quests.funFact: Handrails are placed at a height that children and adults can both reach.

quests.instruction: You are carrying a tall stack of books down the hallway. What is the safest choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Carry less so you can see ahead 📚
options: Rest your chin on top to steady the stack 🙂
Carry less so you can see ahead 📚
Hold the stack tight and walk quickly 🏃
quests.hint: You need to see where you're going.
quests.explanation: If you can't see the path, you could trip or bump into people. Carrying less or asking for help is safer.
quests.funFact: Carrying two smaller piles is often easier than one giant pile.

quests.instruction: How should you carry scissors when you walk with them?
quests.correctAnswer: Closed, with the blades pointing down ✂️
options: In your pocket with the points up 👖
Closed, with the blades pointing down ✂️
Open, with the points up 🔼
quests.hint: Think about protecting yourself and others.
quests.explanation: Carrying scissors closed with the blades down helps prevent cuts if you trip.
quests.funFact: Safety scissors for children have rounded tips.

quests.instruction: You are handing scissors to a classmate. What is the safe way?
quests.correctAnswer: Pass them with the handles toward your classmate 🤝
options: Pass them with the handles toward your classmate 🤝
Pass them with the blades pointing toward them 🔼
Slide them across the table to your classmate 🎯
quests.explanation: Giving the handles first means your classmate can take the scissors without touching the sharp part.
quests.funFact: Never throw scissors or other sharp tools.

quests.instruction: While you cut paper, where should your free hand be?
quests.correctAnswer: Holding the paper away from the blades 🖐️
options: Holding the paper away from the blades 🖐️
Under the paper where you're cutting 🤚
In front of the blades ✋
quests.hint: Keep fingers clear of the blade.
quests.explanation: Holding the paper from the side means your fingers aren't where the blades close.
quests.funFact: Turning the paper rather than the scissors helps you cut curves.

quests.instruction: Why should all four chair legs stay on the floor?
quests.correctAnswer: A tipping chair can fall and hurt you 🪑
options: A tipping chair can fall and hurt you 🪑
The chair would wear out much faster 💰
The chair legs would get scratched and dirty 🧽
quests.explanation: When a chair tips on two legs, it can easily fall back, and you can hit your head.
quests.funFact: A chair is steadiest when all four legs touch the ground.

quests.instruction: Your backpack is in the aisle where classmates walk. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Put it under your desk or in the storage area 🎒
options: Hang it from your chair back 🪑
Put it under your desk or in the storage area 🎒
Leave it, because people can step over it 🚶
quests.explanation: A clear path stops people from tripping, especially in an emergency.
quests.funFact: In an evacuation, clear pathways let everyone get out quickly.

quests.instruction: You can't reach a book on a high shelf. What is the safest thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask your teacher for help 🙋
options: Jump up and pull it ⬆️
Stand on a chair to reach it 🪑
Ask your teacher for help 🙋
quests.explanation: Chairs are not made for standing on and can slip, so ask an adult to reach it.
quests.funFact: Many classrooms have a step stool, and adults can supervise its use.

quests.instruction: Why do we raise our hand before speaking in class?
quests.correctAnswer: So everyone gets a fair turn to be heard ✋
options: So everyone gets a fair turn to be heard ✋
So only the best answers are shared 🏆
So the teacher can count how many are talking 🔢
quests.hint: Think about what happens when everyone shouts at once.
quests.explanation: Taking turns makes sure all voices are heard and nobody gets talked over.
quests.funFact: In some classrooms, students use a 'talking stick' to show whose turn it is.

quests.instruction: A classmate is sharing something with the class. How do you show respect?
quests.correctAnswer: Look at them and wait until they finish 👀
options: Think about your own story while they talk 🗣️
Look at them and wait until they finish 👀
Whisper quietly with a friend nearby 💬
quests.hint: Think about what you'd like when you speak.
quests.explanation: Looking at the speaker and waiting shows you respect them and care about what they say.
quests.funFact: Good listeners remember more of what they hear.

quests.instruction: How can you show you were listening after someone has finished speaking?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask a question about their idea 🤔
options: Say 'okay' and look away 👀
Start talking about something else 🗣️
Ask a question about their idea 🤔
quests.hint: Show you heard what they said.
quests.explanation: A question or comment about their idea shows you were paying attention.
quests.funFact: Paying full attention and responding to a speaker is called active listening.

quests.instruction: Why must you stay inside the playground boundary?
quests.correctAnswer: Adults can see you and keep you safe 👀
options: The grass outside the boundary is wetter 🌱
The equipment outside is too far to reach 🏃
Adults can see you and keep you safe 👀
quests.explanation: Staying in the marked area means teachers can watch over everyone.
quests.funFact: Teachers on playground duty often wear bright vests.

quests.instruction: Why should you not push others on playground equipment?
quests.correctAnswer: Someone could fall and get hurt ⚠️
options: Someone could fall and get hurt ⚠️
It makes equipment dirty 🧼
It makes the game too slow 🐢
quests.explanation: A push can make someone lose their grip or balance and fall from a height.
quests.funFact: Most playground injuries happen from falls.

quests.instruction: Your ball rolls over the fence toward the road. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell the adult on duty and let them help 🙋
options: Climb the fence quickly to fetch the ball 🧗
Tell the adult on duty and let them help 🙋
Check for cars, then run out to get it 🏃
quests.explanation: Never go into the road to fetch a ball. An adult can find a safe way.
quests.funFact: Drivers may not see a child who runs into the road until it is too late to stop.

quests.instruction: The fire alarm rings during a lesson. What should you do first?
quests.correctAnswer: Stop and follow your teacher 🚶
options: Finish the sentence you're writing first ✏️
Stop and follow your teacher 🚶
Pack all your books before you leave 🎒
quests.explanation: Stopping immediately and listening to your teacher gets everyone out safely.
quests.funFact: Fire drills are practiced so that moving out feels familiar.

quests.instruction: Why should you leave your bag behind during an evacuation?
quests.correctAnswer: It saves time and keeps exits clear 🚪
options: Bags are too heavy to carry outside ⚖️
It saves time and keeps exits clear 🚪
Everything in a bag is easy to replace 🙂
quests.explanation: Leaving your things lets you move quickly and keeps the way out from getting blocked.
quests.funFact: Fire drills are usually held a few times each school year.

quests.instruction: After you leave the building in a drill, where do you go?
quests.correctAnswer: To the assembly point and wait with your class 📍
options: Back into the building to collect your coat 🏫
Straight home on your own before roll call 🏠
To the assembly point and wait with your class 📍
quests.explanation: The assembly point is where teachers count their students and make sure everyone is safe.
quests.funFact: Every school has a map showing exits and assembly points.

quests.instruction: Why shouldn't we share our food with classmates at school?
quests.correctAnswer: Some classmates have serious allergies 🥜
options: Shared food gets cold much too quickly 🥶
Some classmates have serious allergies 🥜
Food tastes better when you eat it alone 🍽️
quests.hint: Think about the person who eats it.
quests.explanation: A food that is safe for you might cause a dangerous reaction for someone else.
quests.funFact: Common allergens include nuts, eggs, and milk.

quests.instruction: You need to cough. What is the best way to do it?
quests.correctAnswer: Into your elbow or a tissue 💪
options: Without covering your mouth 😮
Into your hands 🤲
Into your elbow or a tissue 💪
quests.hint: Don't spread germs on your hands.
quests.explanation: Coughing into an elbow keeps germs off your hands, which touch things.
quests.funFact: The 'vampire cough' into your elbow is a common method in schools.

quests.instruction: You used a tissue to blow your nose. Where should it go?
quests.correctAnswer: In the bin 🗑️
options: On your desk 🗄️
Back in your pocket 👖
In the bin 🗑️
quests.explanation: Used tissues go in the bin right away, so the germs don't spread.
quests.funFact: Germs can spread through tiny droplets from coughs and sneezes.

quests.instruction: Why should you keep your password a secret?
quests.correctAnswer: So nobody else can use your account 🔒
options: So nobody else can use your account 🔒
So the computer runs faster ⚡
So friends can log in and help you 🤝
quests.explanation: If someone knows your password, they could read or change your work.
quests.funFact: A strong password is long and hard to guess.

quests.instruction: You see something online that makes you feel uncomfortable. What should you do?
quests.correctAnswer: Close it and tell a teacher or parent 🙋
options: Share the link with friends to ask them 📤
Keep looking to find out what it is 👀
Close it and tell a teacher or parent 🙋
quests.explanation: Telling an adult helps keep you and others safe online.
quests.funFact: Adults at school want to know when something online upsets you.

quests.instruction: You want to take a photo of classmates for a project. What should you do first?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask for permission 📸
options: Post it online right away 🌐
Take it secretly 🤫
Ask for permission 📸
quests.hint: People decide about their own pictures.
quests.explanation: Asking before taking a photo respects privacy.
quests.funFact: Many schools have rules about photos so that students stay safe.

quests.instruction: Why shouldn't you write on classroom desks?
quests.correctAnswer: Desks are shared, and others have to use them 🗄️
options: It makes the desk uncomfortable to sit at 🪑
Desks are shared, and others have to use them 🗄️
It uses up your pencil too quickly ✏️
quests.explanation: Writing on shared things damages them and makes extra work for others.
quests.funFact: Cleaning marks off furniture takes time that could be spent on teaching.

quests.instruction: You accidentally break a classroom item. What is the best thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell your teacher what happened 🙋
options: Tell your teacher what happened 🙋
Quietly hide the pieces in the bin 🗑️
Say a classmate did it by mistake 👈
quests.explanation: Telling the truth lets the teacher fix the problem, and accidents are okay when you're honest.
quests.funFact: Most people forgive an accident much more easily than a lie.

quests.instruction: There is a plant in your classroom that everyone shares. How can you help look after it?
quests.correctAnswer: Water it when asked and be gentle with it 🌱
options: Water it when asked and be gentle with it 🌱
Pick a few leaves to take home 🍃
Move it into the hallway for more light 🚪
quests.explanation: Shared plants need steady, gentle care from everyone.
quests.funFact: Plants need the right amount of water. Too much can harm them.

quests.instruction: During a test, you accidentally glimpse your neighbor's answer. What is the honest thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Look away and give your own answer ✏️
options: Look away and give your own answer ✏️
Change your answer to match theirs 🔄
Whisper to ask if theirs is right 💬
quests.hint: The test should show what you know.
quests.explanation: Giving your own answer shows what you really know, so your teacher can help where you need it.
quests.funFact: Teachers use test results to decide what to teach next.

quests.instruction: Why does doing your own homework matter?
quests.correctAnswer: It helps you learn and practice 📚
options: It always takes much less time to finish ⏱️
It makes your handwriting look neater 🖊️
It helps you learn and practice 📚
quests.explanation: Homework is practice for your own brain.
quests.funFact: Making mistakes in homework tells you what to practice.

quests.instruction: You lost a ruler you borrowed. What is a responsible thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell the owner, say sorry, and offer to replace it 🙏
options: Tell the owner, say sorry, and offer to replace it 🙏
Quietly borrow a similar ruler from someone else 🫳
Wait to see if the owner notices it is gone 🙂
quests.explanation: Telling the truth and offering to make it right shows you take responsibility.
quests.funFact: Saying sorry works best when you also try to fix the problem.
